#!/usr/bin/env bash
# report-leg-failure.sh — the enriched leg-failure notice (gh-1363).
#
# Engine-side factory glue (the flip target of the factory workflow's
# «Link the run back to the issue» step — the bare-link poster). Ships in
# the factory-setup asset next to the other engine scripts; the workflow
# step becomes a thin caller:
#
#   run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-setup/scripts/report-leg-failure.sh"
#
# Behavior contract (gh-1363):
#   success      → the historical bare-link line, byte-identical (AC6 — no
#                  new comments on success paths).
#   unset        → a ::warning:: and no comment at all — a missing OUTCOME
#                  is a misconfiguration, never a fabricated "run success"
#                  (gh-1363 review).
#   otherwise    → ONE enriched comment built by the shipped pure builder
#                  js/common/legFailureReport.js (same factory-setup asset):
#                  phase, failing step name (jobs API), ≤30-line excerpt of
#                  `gh run view --log-failed`, run id + link, the leg-start
#                  pre-flight line when available, and the repeat count
#                  against prior `failure-signature:` lines on the issue.
#   degradation  → every probe failure drops its section, never the notice:
#                  if the builder output cannot be produced at all, the
#                  historical bare-link line is posted as the fallback.
#
# Env block of the calling workflow step (all optional unless noted):
#   NUMBER            issue to comment on (required — absent → exit 0, the
#                     PR-anchored lane has no issue to notice on)
#   OUTCOME           success | failure | cancelled | <other>
#   CI_RUN_URL        run URL (empty → built from GITHUB_* env)
#   PHASE             setup | ai-work | reporting (default ai-work — the
#                     notice covers the whole job; the setup path reports
#                     its own phase through the ticket comment)
#   PREFLIGHT_LINE    the canonical `git pre-flight: …` line captured at leg
#                     start (optional — the report includes it when available)
#   WORKFLOW_FILE     the leg workflow filename for the signature (default
#                     ai-teammate.yml)
#   GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_SERVER_URL, GITHUB_RUN_ID   (runner-provided)
#   GH_TOKEN / SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN  (gh auth, runner-provided)
#
# Rendering rides node (present on GH runners) + the shipped builder —
# ONE canonical implementation of the signature math and the report shape;
# this script is transport only. Payload bytes travel via stdin (never argv
# — E2BIG past 128 KiB, the same rule the token-usage publisher learned):
# the comment history enters the payload through `jq --slurpfile` fed by a
# process substitution, so the largest component never touches argv either.
#
# --self-test: `bash scripts/report-leg-failure.sh --self-test` exercises
# the contract end-to-end with a stub `gh` on PATH (node + jq run for real):
# the success byte-shape, the unset-outcome guard, the enriched failure
# report (incl. repeat count), the >128 KiB comment history (E2BIG rule)
# and the builder-unavailable fallback. Exit 0 only when every scenario
# holds — the advertised verification command actually verifies.
set -u

REPO="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
NUMBER="${NUMBER:-}"
OUTCOME="${OUTCOME:-}"

RUN_URL="${CI_RUN_URL:-}"
if [ -z "$RUN_URL" ] && [ -n "${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-}" ] && [ -n "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-}" ]; then
  RUN_URL="$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$REPO/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID"
fi

KIT_ROOT="${FACTORY_SETUP_ROOT:-$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)}"
KIT_JS="$KIT_ROOT/js/common/legFailureReport.js"
KIT_MARKUP="$KIT_ROOT/js/common/commentMarkup.js"
KIT_SHAPES="$KIT_ROOT/js/common/ticketKeyShapes.js"

# The historical bare-link line via the shipped builder, with a plain-shell
# fallback when node/the kit is unavailable — the notice itself must never
# depend on the enrichment stack. The fallback default keeps both layers
# byte-aligned when no run URL is known (gh-1363 review).
leg_failure_outcome_line() {
  node -e 'const kit = require(process.argv[1]); process.stdout.write(kit.outcomeLine(process.argv[2], process.argv[3]))' \
    "$KIT_JS" "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null \
    || printf '🤖 AI Teammate run %s: %s' "$1" "${2:-<run-url-unavailable>}"
}

# ── --self-test ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# End-to-end contract check with a stub `gh` on PATH (node + jq run for
# real). Covers: the success byte-shape (AC6), the unset-outcome guard, the
# enriched failure report incl. repeat count, the >128 KiB comment history
# (payload never travels argv — E2BIG) and the builder-unavailable fallback.
# Exit 0 only when every scenario holds.
self_test() {
  local fails=0 tmp stubs rec out body rc script
  script="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/$(basename "$0")"
  tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
  stubs="$tmp/stubs"
  mkdir -p "$stubs" "$tmp/no-kit"

  # gh test double: records posted bodies to $GH_STUB_RECORD (separated by a
  # --BOUNDARY-- line), serves canned payloads from the FILES $GH_STUB_JOBS /
  # $GH_STUB_LOG / $GH_STUB_COMENTS point at — a big fixture must not travel
  # env/argv either. jq filters are applied with the real jq, like gh does.
  cat > "$stubs/gh" <<'STUB_EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
REC="${GH_STUB_RECORD:?GH_STUB_RECORD unset}"
case "$1 $2" in
  "issue comment")
    prev=""
    for a in "$@"; do
      if [ "$prev" = "--body-file" ]; then cat >> "$REC"; fi
      if [ "$prev" = "--body" ]; then printf '%s' "$a" >> "$REC"; fi
      prev="$a"
    done
    printf '\n--BOUNDARY--\n' >> "$REC"
    exit 0 ;;
  "run view")
    case "$*" in
      *--log-failed*) [ -n "${GH_STUB_LOG:-}" ] && cat "$GH_STUB_LOG" ;;
      *)
        prev=""
        for a in "$@"; do
          if [ "$prev" = "--jq" ]; then [ -n "${GH_STUB_JOBS:-}" ] && jq -r "$a" < "$GH_STUB_JOBS" 2>/dev/null; fi
          prev="$a"
        done ;;
    esac
    exit 0 ;;
  "issue view")
    prev=""
    for a in "$@"; do
      if [ "$prev" = "--jq" ]; then [ -n "${GH_STUB_COMENTS:-}" ] && jq -c "$a" < "$GH_STUB_COMENTS" 2>/dev/null; fi
      prev="$a"
    done
    exit 0 ;;
esac

  first_body() { sed '/^--BOUNDARY--$/,$d' "$1"; }

  # One scenario invocation of this very script: scrubbed ambient CI env +
  # the stub PATH + per-scenario vars.
  scenario_env() {
    env -u NUMBER -u OUTCOME -u CI_RUN_URL -u PHASE -u PREFLIGHT_LINE \
        -u WORKFLOW_FILE -u GITHUB_REPOSITORY -u GITHUB_SERVER_URL \
        -u GITHUB_RUN_ID -u FACTORY_SETUP_ROOT \
        PATH="$stubs:$PATH" GH_STUB_RECORD="$1" "${@:2}"
  }

  assert_contains() {
    if [ "$2" != "${2#*"$3"}" ]; then
      echo "ok - $1"
    else
      echo "self-test FAIL: $1"
      fails=$((fails + 1))
    fi
  }

  assert_equals() {
    if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then
      echo "ok - $1"
    else
      echo "self-test FAIL: $1 — got [$2]"
      fails=$((fails + 1))
    fi
  }

  # Canned failing-job payload + log excerpt + the matching fixture signature.
  cat > "$tmp/jobs.json" <<'JOBS_EOF'
{"jobs":[{"conclusion":"failure","steps":[{"name":"Build","conclusion":"success"},{"name":"Test","conclusion":"failure"}]}]}
JOBS_EOF
  printf 'log line A\nlog line B' > "$tmp/log.txt"
  if ! sig="$(node -e 'const kit=require(process.argv[1]);process.stdout.write(kit.failureSignature({workflow:"ai-teammate.yml",step:"Test",message:"Test\nlog line A\nlog line B"}))' "$KIT_JS")"; then
    echo "report-leg-failure self-test: FAIL — cannot derive the fixture signature (node/KIT_JS broken)"
    rm -rf "$tmp"
    return 1
  fi
  jq -cn --arg sig "$sig" \
    '{comments: [{author: {login: "bot"}, body: ("older notice\nfailure-signature: " + $sig)}]}' \
    > "$tmp/comments.json"
  # A >128 KiB comment history (MAX_ARG_STRLEN): pad comment first (older),
  # the matching signature line last — the E2BIG-rule fixture.
  node -e 'process.stdout.write("x".repeat(150000))' > "$tmp/pad.txt"
  jq -cn --arg sig "$sig" --rawfile pad "$tmp/pad.txt" \
    '{comments: [{author: {login: "bot"}, body: $pad},
                 {author: {login: "bot"}, body: ("failure-signature: " + $sig)}]}' \
    > "$tmp/comments-big.json"

  # 1 — success keeps the historical bare-link line, byte-exact (AC6).
  rec="$tmp/r1"; : > "$rec"
  out="$(scenario_env "$rec" NUMBER=12 GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets OUTCOME=success \
      CI_RUN_URL=https://github.com/acme/widgets/actions/runs/42 bash "$script" 2>&1)"; rc=$?
  assert_equals "success exits 0" "$rc" "0"
  assert_equals "success posts the bare-link line byte-shape (AC6)" \
    "$(first_body "$rec")" \
    '🤖 AI Teammate run success: https://github.com/acme/widgets/actions/runs/42'

  # 2 — an UNSET outcome is a warning + skipped notice, never a fake success.
  rec="$tmp/r2"; : > "$rec"
  out="$(scenario_env "$rec" NUMBER=12 GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets bash "$script" 2>&1)"; rc=$?
  assert_equals "unset outcome exits 0" "$rc" "0"
  assert_contains "unset outcome warns and skips (nothing fabricated)" \
    "$out$( [ -s "$rec" ] && echo ' POSTED-SOMETHING' )" \
    "::warning::report-leg-failure: OUTCOME unset"
  if [ -s "$rec" ]; then
    echo "self-test FAIL: unset outcome must not post — got [$(cat "$rec")]"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
  else
    echo "ok - unset outcome posts nothing"
  fi

  # 3 — failure renders ONE enriched comment with the repeat count.
  rec="$tmp/r3"; : > "$rec"
  out="$(scenario_env "$rec" NUMBER=12 GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets OUTCOME=failure \
      GITHUB_SERVER_URL=https://github.com GITHUB_RUN_ID=4242 PHASE=ai-work \
      GH_STUB_JOBS="$tmp/jobs.json" GH_STUB_LOG="$tmp/log.txt" \
      GH_STUB_COMENTS="$tmp/comments.json" bash "$script" 2>&1)"; rc=$?
  assert_equals "enriched failure exits 0" "$rc" "0"
  body="$(first_body "$rec")"
  assert_contains "enriched failure carries the report heading" "$body" '### 🤖 AI Teammate run failed'
  assert_contains "enriched failure carries the failing step" "$body" '**Failing step:** Test'
  assert_contains "enriched failure carries the phase" "$body" '**Phase:** ai-work'
  assert_contains "enriched failure carries the bounded excerpt" "$body" 'log line B'
  assert_contains "enriched failure carries the repeat count" "$body" 'identical failure #2 in a row'
  assert_contains "enriched failure carries the signature line" "$body" \
    'failure-signature: ai-teammate.yml | Test |'

  # 4 — a >128 KiB comment history still enriches (payload never on argv).
  rec="$tmp/r4"; : > "$rec"
  out="$(scenario_env "$rec" NUMBER=12 GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets OUTCOME=failure \
      GITHUB_SERVER_URL=https://github.com GITHUB_RUN_ID=4242 PHASE=ai-work \
      GH_STUB_JOBS="$tmp/jobs.json" GH_STUB_LOG="$tmp/log.txt" \
      GH_STUB_COMENTS="$tmp/comments-big.json" bash "$script" 2>&1)"; rc=$?
  assert_equals "E2BIG history exits 0" "$rc" "0"
  body="$(first_body "$rec")"
  assert_contains "150 KiB history still carries the failing step" "$body" '**Failing step:** Test'
  assert_contains "150 KiB history still carries the repeat count (payload off argv)" "$body" \
    'identical failure #2 in a row'

  # 5 — builder unavailable → bare-link fallback keeps the placeholder.
  rec="$tmp/r5"; : > "$rec"
  out="$(scenario_env "$rec" NUMBER=12 GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets OUTCOME=failure \
      FACTORY_SETUP_ROOT="$tmp/no-kit" bash "$script" 2>&1)"; rc=$?
  assert_equals "builder-unavailable exits 0" "$rc" "0"
  assert_equals "fallback keeps the run-url placeholder (never a dangling colon)" \
    "$(first_body "$rec")" '🤖 AI Teammate run failure: <run-url-unavailable>'

  rm -rf "$tmp"
  if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "report-leg-failure self-test: PASS"
    return 0
  fi
  echo "report-leg-failure self-test: FAIL ($fails assertion(s) failed)"
  return 1
}

if [ "${1:-}" = "--self-test" ]; then
  self_test
  exit $?
fi

if [ -z "$NUMBER" ] || [ -z "$REPO" ]; then
  echo "::warning::report-leg-failure: NUMBER/GITHUB_REPOSITORY unset — nothing to notice on"
  exit 0
fi

# AC6 — the success path stays the historical bare-link line. An UNSET
# outcome is never a success: warn and skip (a missing env var must not
# fabricate a "run success" comment — gh-1363 review).
case "$OUTCOME" in
  success)
    gh issue comment "$NUMBER" --repo "$REPO" \
      --body "$(leg_failure_outcome_line success "$RUN_URL")"
    exit $?
    ;;
  '')
    echo "::warning::report-leg-failure: OUTCOME unset — notice skipped"
    exit 0
    ;;
esac

# The failed step name: first failed step of the first failed job.
STEP_NAME="$(gh run view "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-}" --repo "$REPO" --json jobs \
  --jq 'first(.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .steps[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name) // empty' \
  2>/dev/null || true)"
# older gh --jq prints JSON-encoded strings — strip a wrapping pair of quotes
STEP_NAME="${STEP_NAME%\"}"
STEP_NAME="${STEP_NAME#\"}"

# The excerpt: tail of the failed-step log, hard cap 30 (AC5).
EXCERPT="$(gh run view "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-}" --repo "$REPO" --log-failed 2>/dev/null | tail -n 30 || true)"

# Prior signature history: this issue's own comments (existing surface —
# no new persistence), most recent last. A failed/empty read degrades to []
# — every probe failure must drop its section, never kill the notice.
PRIOR_BODIES="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$REPO" --json comments \
  --jq '[.comments[].body]' 2>/dev/null || true)"
PRIOR_BODIES="${PRIOR_BODIES:-[]}"
case "$PRIOR_BODIES" in
  \[*) : ;; # a JSON array — usable
  *) PRIOR_BODIES="[]" ;;
esac

# Build the enriched comment with the shipped builder. Payload via stdin.
NODE_PROG="$(cat <<'PROG_EOF'
const fs = require('fs');
// node -e argv: [node, kitJs, kitMarkup, kitShapes] — user args start at 1.
const kit = require(process.argv[1]);
const markup = require(process.argv[2]);
process.argv[3] && require(process.argv[3]);
const env = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8'));
const signature = kit.failureSignature({
  workflow: env.workflow, step: env.step, message: env.message
});
const repeat = kit.consecutiveRepeatCount(
  signature, kit.parseSignatureLines(env.priorBodies));
const body = kit.buildFailureComment({
  phase: env.phase,
  step: env.step,
  runId: env.runId,
  runUrl: env.runUrl,
  preflightLine: env.preflightLine,
  excerpt: env.excerpt,
  repeatCount: repeat,
  signature: signature
}, markup.forFlavor('markdown'));
process.stdout.write(body);
PROG_EOF
)"

# PRIOR_BODIES — the whole comment history, the largest payload component —
# enters through --slurpfile + process substitution: argv carries only an
# fd path, so a >128 KiB history cannot hit E2BIG (the stdin rule this
# script exists on). `|| echo '{}'` keeps the bare-link fallback for a
# broken read, as before.
PAYLOAD="$(jq -n \
  --arg workflow "${WORKFLOW_FILE:-ai-teammate.yml}" \
  --arg step "${STEP_NAME:-}" \
  --arg message "${STEP_NAME:-}
$EXCERPT" \
  --arg phase "${PHASE:-ai-work}" \
  --arg runId "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-}" \
  --arg runUrl "$RUN_URL" \
  --arg preflightLine "${PREFLIGHT_LINE:-}" \
  --arg excerpt "$EXCERPT" \
  --slurpfile priorBodies <(printf '%s' "$PRIOR_BODIES") \
  '{workflow: $workflow, step: $step, message: $message, phase: $phase,
    runId: $runId, runUrl: $runUrl, preflightLine: $preflightLine,
    excerpt: $excerpt} * {priorBodies: $priorBodies[0]}' || echo '{}')"

BODY="$(printf '%s' "${PAYLOAD:-{\}}" | node -e "$NODE_PROG" "$KIT_JS" "$KIT_MARKUP" "$KIT_SHAPES" 2>/dev/null || true)"

if [ -n "$BODY" ]; then
  printf '%s' "$BODY" | gh issue comment "$NUMBER" --repo "$REPO" --body-file - && exit 0
  echo "::warning::report-leg-failure: enriched notice posting failed — falling back to the bare link"
else
  echo "::warning::report-leg-failure: enriched notice unavailable (node/builder failure) — bare-link fallback"
fi

# Fallback: never lose the notice entirely.
gh issue comment "$NUMBER" --repo "$REPO" \
  --body "$(leg_failure_outcome_line "$OUTCOME" "$RUN_URL")"

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instructionOverrides.<contextId>` — replace `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `agentParamPatches.<contextId>` — patch `agentParams` fields for a specific agent
- `globalCliPrompts` — prompt files appended to **every** agent's CLI input (inject-to-all)
- `globalAdditionalInstructions` — instruction files appended to **every** agent's `agentParams.instructions`

**Example — inject codegraph into all agents without repeating per context:**
```js
// .dmtools/config.js
module.exports = {
    globalCliPrompts: [
        './agents/instructions/common/codegraph_tools.md'
    ],
    cliPrompts: {
        story_development: ['./.dmtools/prompts/development_focus.md'],
        pr_review:         ['./.dmtools/prompts/review_focus.md']
        // codegraph_tools.md is injected automatically into all agents above
    }
};
```

Global entries are merged **after** per-agent entries so they always appear last.

### SM rules override and custom agents
`js/smAgent.js` supports full and partial SM customization from `.dmtools/config.js`.

**Precedence**
- Base rules come from `sm.json` (`jobParams.rules`)
- If `config.smRules` is set, it **fully replaces** base rules
- If `config.smRuleOverrides` is set, it patches rules by `configFile`

**Common use cases**
- Disable most default rules and keep only one:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    "agents/story_questions.json": { enabled: true },
    "agents/story_development.json": { enabled: false },
    "agents/pr_review.json": { enabled: false }
  }
};
```

- Full replacement with custom agents:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRules: [
    {
      description: "Run only custom intake flow",
      jql: "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype = Story AND status = 'To Do'",
      configFile: "agents/my_custom_intake.json",
      skipIfLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      addLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      enabled: true
    }
  ]
};
```

**Rule fields supported by SM**
- `description`, `jql`, `configFile` (required for practical execution)
- `enabled` (set `false` to disable)
- `skipIfLabel` / `skipIfLabels`, `addLabel`
- `targetStatus`, `limit`, `localExecution`
- `configPath` (per-rule project config override for multi-project orchestration)

### Figma design lookup
Any agent that writes or reviews requirements-facing content (questions, descriptions, acceptance criteria, solution/design analysis, dev/test scoping) must treat the linked Figma design as a primary source, not an optional nice-to-have — a story/question/AC that ignores an available design is incomplete, the same way ignoring the code would be.

- **If a ticket/story already links a specific Figma file or node** (a `/file/` or `/design/` URL, optionally with `node-id`): open it directly with `figma_get_file_structure` / `figma_get_layers` / `figma_download_image_of_file` (see `instructions/common/media_handling.md`) before writing output.
- **If only a team- or project-level Figma URL is known** (e.g. a `.../team/<teamId>/...` "files" listing link, typically stored as project config rather than on the ticket itself): resolve it top-down with `figma_list_team_projects` → `figma_list_project_files` to find the file matching the current feature/epic, then drill into it as above. Match by file name against the feature/epic name; if no file name matches, say so explicitly rather than silently skipping the design check.
- **If the design is genuinely unavailable** (no link resolves, access error, no matching file after searching): say so explicitly in the output instead of proceeding as if no design existed — this is the same "unavailable artifact" handling already required by `instructions/common/acceptance_criteria_quality.md`.
- Never fabricate UI/UX details (copy, layout, states) that should come from Figma — pull them from the design or ask a question, don't guess.
- This is process guidance, not a project config — the actual team/project URLs and file-naming convention for a given product live in that product's `.dmtools/instructions/goal/goal.md` or `.dmtools/config.js`, never here.

### Output JSON discipline
When agents produce JSON output files, keep them compact (status, IDs, paths, short summaries). Put large text in separate `.md` files and reference them by path.

### Path stability
Do not rename or move root `*.json` config files — CI workflows and Jira automations reference them by path. Safe refactors: splitting prompt markdown, adding instruction files, adding `cliPrompts` composition in target repos.

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Duplication gate (production JS duplicated lines <= 1%, ratcheted)
        # Ratchet, not an absolute bar: a pinned set of production JS files
        # already exceeds 1% duplicated lines — pre-existing debt owned by the
        # gh-1244…gh-1250 dedup tickets (see duplication-baseline.json for the
        # current pinned set) — so the measurement's exit 2 is expected for
        # now. The baseline pins each over-threshold file with its measured
        # percentage and absolute duplicated-line count; the gate FAILS only
        # on a NEW over-threshold file or a pinned file that gained ABSOLUTE
        # duplicated lines (ci/duplicationRatchet.js) — a percentage shift
        # caused by file shrinkage passes and is logged as informational —
        # keeping the absolute 1% bar as the end state once the debt lands.
        # A crashed measurement (tool exit other than 0/2) never passes.
        # js/unit-tests/** stays excluded; the badge step below reparses the
        # same measurement for the README endpoint.
        run: |
          set +e
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" duplicates --threshold 1 --exclude "js/unit-tests/**" js ci > "$RUNNER_TEMP/dup-gate.txt" 2>&1
          code=$?
          set -e
          node ci/duplicationRatchet.js "$RUNNER_TEMP/dup-gate.txt" duplication-baseline.json "$code"

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e

a) `normalizeSignature` order of operations: URLs first, then `\S*/\S*` path-like tokens. Note: `\S*\/\S*` strips ANY token containing a slash — including... `a/b`. But what about words like "and/or"? That gets stripped entirely too. That's fine for signature stability (over-normalization risk: two different errors could normalize to the same signature → false "identical failure" counts). E.g. "Checkout failed: refs/remotes/origin/main missing" vs "Fetch failed: origin/main unborn" — both strip path-like tokens... The ticket AC3 says SHAs/paths/timestamps must normalize away; over-normalization is inherent to the approach. Not a defect.

b) `\b[0-9a-fA-F]{7,39}\b` strips ALL hex words 7-39 chars — including ordinary words that are all hex chars ≥7 letters like "deadbef", "facade", "cabbage"... "cabbage" is 7 chars all a-f! Real English words like "defaced", "befcake"... hmm "feedback" has 'k' and 't' — no. "acede" 6. "defaced" 7 chars — d,e,f,a,c,e,d all hex! Would be stripped from the signature. Minor over-normalization — cosmetic, signature-stability only. Not worth a finding? It only affects repeat-count accuracy marginally. Maybe a NIT/SUGESTION. Actually, this is a "false positive repeat" risk: two DIFFERENT error messages that both consist of stripped tokens collapse to the same signature → count increments wrongly. E.g. "defaced badge detected" → all words: "defaced" (hex 7) stripped, "badge" (5, kept), "detected" kept. Not fully. The message keeps non-hex words. The risk is small. # Draft issue 01 — Failure reports that carry context: phase, log excerpt, repeat count

Effort: S · Blocks: 02 (failure-analyzer reads exactly this data)

## Problem

When an agent leg fails, the only notification is a bare link:

```
🤖 AI Teammate run failure: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/<id>
```

No failing step, no log excerpt, no phase, no repeat indicator. During the
2026-11-04 incident (a tracked runtime artifact blocking every dev-leg
checkout), **~15 legs failed identically over ~10 hours** and each posted the
same information-free comment — diagnosing the root cause required opening
run logs one by one and pattern-matching by hand.

## Proposed change

Enrich every leg-failure report with bounded, structured context:

0. **Pre-flight state line** (folded from the separate pre-flight-log idea) —
   at leg start, before the first git operation, emit one canonical line:
   `git pre-flight: branch=<b> head=<sha> dirty=<n> staged=<n> paths=[up to 5 + "+N more"]`
   (from `git status --porcelain` + `git rev-parse`; capped length, paths
   only, never file contents). The report includes it when available — it is
   the one thing a post-hoc analyzer can never reconstruct, since the
   workspace state at failure time is gone by the time anyone reads the log.
1. **Phase** — which stage failed: `setup` (clone/checkout/branch — the
   preCliDevelopmentSetup boundary), `ai-work` (the agent's implementation
   session), or `reporting` (post-work bookkeeping). The phase is known at
   the failure site; carry it, don't infer it from the log.
2. **Failing step name** — the workflow step id that failed.
3. **Log excerpt** — the last ~10 lines of the failed step's log
   (`gh run view --log-failed`, trimmed); hard cap ~30 lines; tokens are
   already masked by Actions (`***`) — keep it that way.
4. **Run link + run id.**
5. **Repeat count** — when the previous failures of the same issue+workflow
   share a *normalized signature* (workflow + step name + error message with
   SHAs, paths, timestamps, run ids, URLs stripped), append
   `identical failure #N in a row`; otherwise `first failure with this
   signature`. The signature normalizer is a pure function — unit-testable.

The report stays ONE comment (same place as today), just with content.

## Implementation pointers

- Failure notice step in `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` (currently the
  bare-link poster) + the in-leg setup failure path
  (`js/preCliDevelopmentSetup.js` → the `Development Setup Error` ticket
  comment) should share one report builder.
- New pure helpers (signature normalization, excerpt trimming) live in a small
  `js/common/legFailureReport.js` with unit tests; keep every function's CRAP
  score ≤ 8.
- Signature history: derive from recent failed runs of the same workflow
  (GitHub API), not from a new stored state — no new persistence surface.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A failing leg produces a report containing: phase, failing step name,
   ≤ 30-line log excerpt, run id + link.
2. Two consecutive failures with the same normalized signature → second
   report shows `identical failure #2 in a row`; a different signature →
   `first failure with this signature`.
3. SHAs, run ids, timestamps, and URLs do not leak into the signature
   (normalized away) — unit test with two genuinely-different crashes that
   share only the error class, and one crash whose message embeds a SHA.
4. No secrets in excerpts (Actions masking verified in a test fixture with a
   fake token).
5. Report size bounded (excerpt cap enforced by a test).
6. Existing behavior preserved: no new comments on success paths.

## Out of scope

Acting on the report (parking, analyzing) — that is issue 02. This issue only
makes the report informative.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the log excerpt is byte-unbounded and travels jq argv twice — a >128 KiB excerpt line reproduces E2BIG and posts a junk `failure-signature: |  | ` comment instead of the bare-link fallback**

The F3 fix moved `priorBodies` off argv, but the *excerpt* — now the largest payload component after a verbose failed step — still travels argv on this line, twice (`--arg message "${STEP_NAME:-}
$EXCERPT"` above embeds it too). `trimLogExcerpt` caps **lines** only (`EXCERPT_MAX_LINES = 30`); line width is unbounded, and a single >128 KiB log line (giant command echo, base64/JSON dump — common in Actions logs) sails through the cap.

**Reproduced end-to-end** on this head with a stub `gh` serving a 200 KB single-line failed-step log (`scripts/report-leg-failure.sh`, `OUTCOME=failure`, canned jobs/comments):

```
scripts/report-leg-failure.sh: line 345: /usr/bin/jq: Argument list too long

POSTED BODY:
### 🤖 AI Teammate run failed
**Repeat:** first failure with this signature
failure-signature:  |  |
```

Three defects in one causal chain:

1. **E2BIG** — the excerpt breaks the script's own header rule (`:44-46` "Payload bytes travel via stdin (never argv — E2BIG past 128 KiB)"), exactly the rule F3 established.
2. **`|| echo '{}'` (`:345`) swallows the failure** — and unlike the other probe failures (which drop *sections*), the `{}` payload still renders a "successful" body: the heading, plus a `Repeat:` line and a junk `failure-signature: |  | ` line derived from all-undefined fields. This violates the header's degradation contract (`:21-23` "every probe failure drops its section, never the notice") *and* the ticket's own "never guessed" principle (a fabricated repeat phrase on a report that carries nothing else).
3. **History pollution** — the junk signature line lands on the issue, so the next total-payload-failure counts as `identical failure #2 in a row` against ` |  | ` — a false repeat count.

Suggested fixes (any one stops the junk post; (1)+(2) also keep the enrichment):

1. Byte-cap the excerpt in `trimLogExcerpt` (per-line + total chars — `SIGNATURE_MAX_CHARS` precedent), so no caller can build an oversized payload;
2. Route the excerpt through stdin/`--slurpfile` like `priorBodies` (data never on argv);
3. Treat a `{}`/field-less payload as builder-unavailable → bare-link fallback (e.g. `if [ "${PAYLOAD:-}" = "{}" ]` → skip the enriched post entirely).

A regression test pins it the same way scenario 4 pins the F3 fix: serve a >128 KiB single-line log and assert either an enriched body with a capped excerpt **or** the byte-exact bare-link fallback — never a body carrying `failure-signature:  |  | `.

💡 **SUGGESTION: the production caller of this script lives outside this repo and the flip is untracked — owner review point 3, still open**

This header documents the intended production wiring — `run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-setup/scripts/report-leg-failure.sh"` as the flip target of the engine-side factory workflow's «Link the run back to the issue» step. Nothing in this repo calls the script yet (the bare-link poster is engine-side — confirmed: no workflow in `.github/` posts the historical line), so until the flip lands, the enriched-notice path this PR ships (script + `FACTORY_SETUP_JS` pack carry + self-test) is production-dead code, and ticket AC1 is only satisfiable by the engine repo.

The owner's pre-merge review on this PR explicitly asked for exactly one thing here: *"point 3 needs a tracking issue, not a code change."* Nothing was tracked: the PR description doesn't reference a flip issue, gh-1363's body doesn't, and the epic gh-1362 body doesn't mention the engine-side flip either (checked the repo's open issues — no flip-tracking issue exists).

Since the engine repo is outside this PR's reach, the actionable item here is documentation + tracking, not code:

- reference (or create) the tracking issue for the engine-side flip in this PR description or the gh-1362 epic body, so the shipped flip-target doesn't stay bare forever and gh-1363 can't close with AC1 unmet in production.

No code change requested for this thread.

💡 **SUGGESTION: once the engine-side flip lands, a failed leg posts TWO signatures per cycle — the interleaving pins both repeat counts at "first failure"**

This deliberate separation ("a setup failure and a workflow-step failure of the same ticket never collapse into one repeat count") is right for identity, but it interacts badly with `consecutiveRepeatCount`'s streak semantics (`legFailureReport.js:88` — *a non-matching entry breaks the streak*) once both surfaces fire for the same failed leg, which the script header explicitly plans for (`PHASE` doc: "the notice covers the whole job; the setup path reports its own phase through the ticket comment"):

1. Setup fails → setup-error comment posts signature `A` (`workflow='preCliDevelopmentSetup' | step | msg`); the job then fails → the engine notice posts signature `B` (`workflow='ai-teammate.yml' | …`).
2. Next leg: setup fails again → priors are `[…, A, B]` — the trailing prior is `B` ≠ `A`, so the streak breaks and the report says **"first failure with this signature"** — forever, on both surfaces, for every recurring failure.

That silently defeats ticket AC2 (`ticket.md` — *"second report shows `identical failure #2 in a row`"*) under the planned wiring — precisely the incident scenario gh-1363 exists for (~15 identical legs over 10 hours would each still read "first failure"). Today, pre-flip, only the setup surface exists in this repo, so nothing shipped is broken; this is a design decision to make before the flip, not a live bug.

Cheap fix, testable here: filter priors by workflow (or count per-surface streaks — `signature.split(' | ')[0]` match) before the consecutive count, e.g. pass `parseSignatureLines(...).filter(inSameWorkflow)` into `consecutiveRepeatCount`, and pin it with a test whose prior history interleaves `B, A, B, A` and expects the next `A` to count `#3`.

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: All nine rework threads verified fixed with citable hunks and real regression tests; the `crap` gate is green on head `b828b3c03` (CI `crap` job PASS, plus an independent local replication with the exact CI recipe exiting 0 — 0 new over threshold). One new important issue: the log excerpt is byte-unbounded and travels jq argv, so a >128 KiB excerpt line reproduces E2BIG and posts a junk `failure-signature: |  | ` comment instead of degrading to the bare link (reproduced end-to-end).

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ excerpt byte-cap + argv gap → `jq: Argument list too long` swallowed by `|| echo '{}'` → junk-enriched comment posted (scripts/report-leg-failure.sh:341)
- 💡 engine-side flip of the notice script is still untracked — owner review point 3, nothing references a tracking issue (PR description, gh-1363, gh-1362 all checked)
- 💡 once both failure surfaces fire per leg, their interleaved signatures break the repeat streak on every cycle — AC2 silently pinned at "first failure" (js/preCliDevelopmentSetup.js:554)

**Digest** (💡/🪶 overflow, ranked):
- js/unit-tests/test_workingDir.js — 18 `legFailureReport` stub entries, several in `loadModule` maps of modules that never require it (`configLoader`-only / `outputFiles` / post loads) — dead stub noise (carried unchanged from the prior round's digest)
- js/common/legFailureReport.js:59-60 — `normalizeSignature` also strips ≥7-char all-hex English words (`defaced`) and any token containing `/` (`and/or`) — marginally over-normalizes; repeat-count fidelity only
- js/common/legFailureReport.js:113-128 — `parseSignatureLines` scans every line of every comment, including *quoted* failure reports in human replies — a quoted signature line inflates the repeat count by one

**Verified this round**: `node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js` over the three PR suites — 166 passed, 0 failed; `bash scripts/report-leg-failure.sh --self-test` — 17/17 assertions, exit 0; the lone `sessionDelta` UT-3 AC3 failure under the full suite reproduces identically on clean `f3183be` with `FA_SESSION_ROOT` exported and passes on this head without it — pre-existing and environment-dependent, confirming the PR description's claim.

**Next Steps**:
1. Byte-cap the excerpt in `trimLogExcerpt` (per-line + total), route it via stdin/`--slurpfile` like `priorBodies`, and treat a `{}` payload as builder-unavailable → bare-link fallback; pin with a >128 KiB single-line-log regression test
2. Reference or create the tracking issue for the engine-side workflow flip (AC1's production path)
3. Filter prior signatures by workflow before the consecutive count; add an interleaved-history test
